 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. A comeback attempt by Baylor women's soccer came up short on Saturday as it fell 3-2 to BYU in the Big 12 tournament championship game.
 The Cougars opened the scoring in the 26th minute following a missed clearance by the Bears on a corner kick. The ball bounced to midfielder Lucy Kesler, who fired a left-footed shot off the crossbar. Forward Mattyn Summers-Oviatt was there to put the ricochet into the back of the net for a 1-0 BYU lead.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Cougars extended their lead early in the second half, when a shot from midfielder Mika Krommenhoek struck a Baylor defender's arm inside the 18-yard box for a handball. Defender Bella Woods buried the penalty kick to give BYU a 2-0 advantage.
 In the 55th minute, midfielder Noelle Sather broke through for the Bears with a one-touch shot into the bottom right corner of the net, making the score 2-1. Summers-Oviatt scored again in the 76th minute to give the Cougars a 3-1 advantage.
 Baylor responded in the 78th minute with a goal from forward Lauren Omholt, cutting BYU's lead to 3-2 and setting up a frantic ending with the trailing side pushing numbers forward for an equalizer. BYU's defense, however, held strong to secure the conference title.
